title: architecture review - kv cache sharding meeting notes
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — KV cache sharding (follow-up to RFC-142)
Date: 2026-03-03
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime
Attendees: Ava Chen (chair), Diego Martinez, Riley Thompson, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Patel

Purpose:
- Review outstanding design questions from RFC-142 and capture decisions for implementation and rollout.

Agenda:
1) Recap of RFC-142 goals and constraints
2) Shard key and partitioning strategy
3) Rebalancing and migration plan (state movement)
4) Hot-shard mitigation / throttling / backpressure
5) Observability and metrics to collect
6) Rollout plan and safety gates
7) Open action items and owners

Notes & Discussion:
1) Recap
- RFC-142 aims to horizontally scale the in-memory KV cache used by the serving runtime to reduce cold starts and repeated KV recomputation across high-throughput workloads. Primary constraints: low-latency lookups (<1ms median), ability to scale shards independently, and bounded memory per process.
- Recent benchmarks (PR #1874) show 12–18% tail-latency improvement with sharded cache vs baseline when batch sizes > 8; large variance for skewed key distributions was observed.

2) Shard key and partitioning strategy
- Options considered: model-only, model+session, prefix hashing of prompt, consistent-hash on (model, user-id, prefix).
- Decision: use consistent hashing on a composite key of (model-id, prefix-hash, routing-version) with virtual nodes. Rationale:
  - model-id alone causes collisions for multi-tenant hot prefixes; including prefix-hash (first N bytes of normalized prompt) reduces hot-key collisions while remaining deterministic.
  - routing-version (a lightweight header) allows safe migration between shard layouts and enables sticky routing during rollout.
  - Virtual nodes (128 replicas) to smooth load distribution across shards.
- Action: define canonical prefix normalization (strip whitespace, lowercase, truncate to 256 chars) and document in code + RFC update. Owner: Riley (INF-2345).

3) Rebalancing and migration plan
- Two migration modes discussed: draining + state transfer vs. lazy rebuild on first miss.
- Decision: hybrid approach: initial canary using lazy rebuild (safer, less network traffic) followed by controlled state transfer for full rollout to maintain cold-miss rates.
  - Canary: enable new shard layout on 1–2 dedicated nodes in staging/dedicated pool; routing-version header set per-request. Monitor miss-rate and tail latency for 48h.
  - Full rollout: use background state transfer job that copies hot keys from old shards to new ones. Transfer will prioritize top-N keys by access frequency.
- Action: implement state-transfer tool (background worker) with throttling and metrics. Owner: Diego (JIRA-INF-2391).

4) Hot-shard mitigation / backpressure
- Identified risk: certain prefixes (system prompts, popular templates) cause hot shards and degrade latency.
- Mitigation strategies: client-side prefix caching hints, adaptive replication of hot keys (replicate top-K keys to additional shards), and per-shard token-bucket rate limiting.
- Decision: implement adaptive replication for top-100 hot keys per model and integrate per-shard request queue length + rejection metric to trigger temporary replication. Rejection should be a soft-fail that falls back to cold compute path.
- Action: prototype replication controller and add RL-based policy TBD in a follow-up spike. Owner: Priya.

5) Observability and metrics
- Must capture per-shard metrics: lookup latency histogram, miss-rate, per-key access frequency (approximate via Count-Min sketch), memory utilization, state-transfer throughput, GC pauses.
- Decision: add the following metrics (exposed via Prometheus): kv_shard_lookup_count, kv_shard_lookup_latency_ms_bucket, kv_shard_miss_count, kv_shard_memory_bytes, kv_state_transfer_bytes, kv_hotkey_replication_count.
- Also add tracing spans for routing decision, cache lookup, and state transfer; tag spans with routing-version and shard-id.
- Action: SRE instrumentation ticket and dashboards. Owner: Liam.

6) Rollout plan and safety gates
- Canary phase (staging): enable routing-version header on 5% of traffic to dedicated canary nodes. Evaluate for 48h.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple days with automated rollback on SLA regressions (tail latency or increase in miss-rate beyond thresholds).
- Safety gates:
  - 99th-percentile latency must not increase by >10% vs baseline on canary nodes.
  - Miss-rate increase must be <2% absolute.
  - State-transfer error rate <0.1%.
- Decision: include automatic rollback hook in rollout automation if any gate is breached.
- Action: Add rollout playbook and rollback runbook. Owner: Sofia.

7) Backwards compatibility & client changes
- Introduce a routing-version header; servers will default to v0 if absent. Clients should be able to opt-in for new routing by setting header. For internal clients (hosted-api) the gateway will inject header during canary.
- Ensure old clients without header continue to function (no forced migration).
- Action: update SDKs and gateway injection logic. Owner: Ava / SDK team.

Decisions summary:
- Use consistent hashing on (model-id, prefix-hash, routing-version) with virtual nodes.
- Hybrid migration: lazy rebuild for canary, then controlled state transfer for full rollout.
- Adaptive replication for hot keys + per-shard rate limits for backpressure.
- Instrumentation: add a focused set of per-shard metrics and traces.
- Rollout: staged canary with automated rollback on SLO breach.

Action items (short list):
- Riley: Define canonical prefix normalization and update RFC-142 (INF-2345).
- Diego: Implement state-transfer background worker and proof-of-concept (JIRA-INF-2391).
- Priya: Prototype adaptive hot-key replication controller (ticket TBD).
- Liam: Add Prometheus metrics and initial dashboards for shard health (INF-2412).
- Sofia: Draft rollout playbook and rollback runbook; coordinate with SRE.
- Ava/SDK team: Add routing-version header support to gateway and SDKs; coordinate opt-in for canary.

Next steps / follow-up meetings:
- Spike review in 1 week: Priya and Diego present prototypes for replication controller and state-transfer.
- Rollout readiness review scheduled after canary results (target date: 2026-03-20).

Notes / references:
- See RFC-142 for original design and alternatives considered: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/RFC-142+-+KV+Cache+Sharding
- Benchmarks & PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1874
- Related notes: architecture-review-kv-cache-routing-notes-2026-02-26.json (drive)

End of notes.
